unit.title: Numbers and Operations Around Us
unit.about_unit: Explores how human travel, trade, measurement, and recording large quantities led to five-digit numbers (ten thousands), multi-digit multiplication, division arrays, and multiplicative reasoning.

facilitation_guide.headline: Real-World Contexts
facilitation_guide.text: Connect numbers with train tickets, odometer readings, and village populations.

facilitation_guide.headline: Base-10 Manipulatives
facilitation_guide.text: Emphasize grouping 10 of any unit into 1 of the next higher unit using visual tokens.

chapter.title: Boxes and Arrays
chapter.tagline: Unpacking division and multiplication facts, fact families, and equal sharing arrays
chapter.overview: Observing an organized array of 35 coconuts at the roadside market, children discover that one multiplication fact (5 × 7 = 35) instantly reveals two division facts (35 ÷ 7 = 5 and 35 ÷ 5 = 7). They master the vocabulary of Dividend, Divisor, and Quotient.

sections.title: The Coconut Array: Multiplication & Division Twins
sections.subtitle: Seeing division as the inverse operation of multiplication

storyNarrative.dialogue: I stacked 35 coconuts in 7 neat rows of 5! That tells us 5 × 7 = 35, and also that 35 coconuts shared among 7 customers gives each 5!

concept.heading: Inverse Operations Principle
concept.keyRule: If A × B = C, then C ÷ A = B and C ÷ B = A.

sections.title: Dividend, Divisor, and Quotient: Fact Family Houses
sections.subtitle: Standard terminology for division equations

storyNarrative.dialogue: In 35 ÷ 5 = 7: 35 is the Dividend (the total to split), 5 is the Divisor (the group size), and 7 is the Quotient (the number of groups)!

concept.heading: Division Architecture
concept.keyRule: Dividend (N) ÷ Divisor (D) = Quotient (Q) [where N = D × Q + Remainder].

sections.title: Equal Grouping, Packaging & Word Problems
sections.subtitle: Applying division with remainders to packaging scenarios

storyNarrative.dialogue: If we have 50 sweet boxes and each carton holds 6 boxes, how many full cartons can we pack, and how many are left over?

concept.heading: Division with Remainder
concept.keyRule: 50 ÷ 6 = 8 with a remainder of 2 (8 full cartons, 2 leftover boxes).
